caption: Brendan Ngwa Nforbi v. Diamond Truck Sales, Inc.
claims: Fraudulent Concealment, Intentional Misrepresentation, Negligent Misrepresentation, Breach of Contract, UCL §17200, Rescission & Restitution, Declaratory Relief
status: Active — June 15, 2026 CIV-100 against Diamond and Alpine docketed Not Entered; complete corrected default packets for Diamond and Alpine (separate CIV-100s) mailed July 31, 2026 via USPS Priority Mail (tracking 9505 5114 6005 6212 9832 68; expected delivery 08/03/2026) — see commit/packet PDFs corrected per clerk rejection; clerk stated by phone that the 08/12/2026 CMC will be converted to a default prove-up hearing; Dept. 11B, Hon. Robert T. Waters, 8:30 AM. PLANNED — COURTESY COPIES TO DEFENDANTS AUGUST 4, 2026: Plaintiff intends to mail courtesy copies of the renewed default judgment packets (already mailed to the court Jul. 31, 2026) directly to Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. and Alpine Truck Sales, Inc. Neither defendant has appeared or is represented by counsel, so this is not a required service — a professional courtesy giving both defendants notice of the pending default judgment request before the Aug. 12, 2026 prove-up. Not legally required and does not restart any deadline or waive default. SUPPLEMENTAL MAILING TO THE COURT — AUGUST 3, 2026: per USPS eReceipt (Milpitas Post Office), a second tracked Priority Mail Flat Rate Envelope (tracking 9505 5114 6003 6215 9407 65, $12.90, mailed 11:22 AM PT, est. delivery Aug. 5, 2026) was sent to the San Joaquin Superior Court in Stockton, distinct from the Jul. 31, 2026 mailing (tracking 9505 5114 6005 6212 9832 68), containing the default judgment packet(s) together with a self-addressed stamped envelope (SASE) requesting the clerk return processed/file-stamped copies. Exact scope (Diamond, Alpine, or both) not fully specified as of this writing; likely the Aug. 4, 2026 compensatory-only packets listed below, sent a day ahead of that label.
defendants: Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. (California corporation operating at multiple locations including Texas and South Carolina); Alpine Truck Sales, Inc. (California corporation; 1201 S Soderquist Road, Turlock, CA 95380); DOES 1-20
causes: Violation of Unfair Competition Law, B&P Code §17200 (Count 5)
key_facts: On April 4, 2023, Plaintiff purchased a 2014 Volvo VNL diesel semi-truck (VIN: 4V4NC9EH6EN142206) from Diamond for $26,900.00 (total charges $27,092.75) with >$12,000 down payment and remaining balance financed by third-party lender. At time of sale, truck suffered a severe DEF/emissions system defect affecting the selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system, rendering it non-compliant with California emissions regulations and unsafe for highway operation. The pleadings allege on information and belief that Diamond concealed and failed to disclose: (1) the emissions defect; (2) the truck's regulatory non-compliance; (3) a prior owner's written or verbal disclosure of the DEF system failure and engine derate condition before resale; and (4) a California enforcement agency out-of-service designation. The prior-owner disclosure and enforcement designation remain unconfirmed and subject to investigation and discovery. Shortly after purchase while operating under Lease-On Owner Operator Agreement, truck experienced catastrophic emissions failure, entered 'limp mode,' emitted excessive black smoke, became incapable of exceeding approximately 35 mph, rendering it commercially unusable and unsafe. Plaintiff unable to mitigate by renting/purchasing replacement vehicle due to capital exhaustion. Per the Declaration in Support of Default Judgment (Attachment 4b to the July 20, 2026 CM-110 Case Management Statement), documented out-of-pocket losses total $20,218.65: deposit (Retail Buyer's Order) $12,345.10; GAP Addendum enrollment $1,895.00; CA DMV fees $3,442.00 (billed, outstanding, penalties accruing); Brannon Tire (emergency tire/road service) $1,197.34; Mobile Will's Truck/Auto Repair Shop $740.00; Golden Empire Towing, Inc. $562.50; Western Truck Center (lamp/parts) $36.71. Additional undocumented out-of-pocket losses (sworn testimony, no receipt) total $5,750.00: Commercial Towing (CVC §22852 storage release) $750.00; Almaraz Diesel (DEF/SCR diagnostic and repair) $5,000.00. Lost commercial income for the default prove-up is conservatively calculated at $23,400.00 (18 weeks × $1,300/week) — a deliberately conservative sworn figure distinct from the broader >$46,800 projected lost-income theory pursued against both defendants at trial. Prejudgment interest under Civ. Code §3287(a) (7%, ~3.04 years) adds $4,302.55, for a compensatory subtotal of $53,671.20, plus $25,000.00 in punitive damages under Civ. Code §3294 — a default judgment prove-up total of not less than $78,671.20 plus costs of suit, sought against Diamond alone.
procedural_status: Filed 02/13/2026 (pro se, fee waiver approved). Summons issued. Diamond Truck Sales Inc. served 03/11/2026 via POS-010; response due 04/10/2026; no response filed. Diamond re-served with the Amended Summons/First Amended Complaint 05/12/2026; no response filed. Request for Entry of Default and Default Court Judgment (CIV-100) submitted 06/15/2026 at 9:00 A.M. naming both Diamond and Alpine — ROA CODEDEFAULT: Not Entered (Alpine had not yet been served; clerk issued CIV-100 Notice to Filing Party). Alpine Truck Sales, Inc. personally served July 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM — Mustagem Usmani (Manager), 1201 S Soderquist Road, Turlock, CA 95380; served by San Joaquin County Sheriff Deputy T. Caldwell under CCP §416.10 (corporation); documents served: Amended Summons, First Amended Complaint, Notice of Case Assignment and Notice of Hearing; POS-010 signed July 2, 2026 by Sheriff's Authorized Agent Jeff Dirkse (Levying Officer File No. 2026002577; $50 fee waived). Alpine response deadline: July 31, 2026 (CCP §412.20(a)(3)). On July 31, 2026 at 12:50 PM — after Alpine's July 31 response deadline under CCP §412.20(a)(3) — Plaintiff printed, signed, and mailed complete renewed default judgment packets for both Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. and Alpine Truck Sales, Inc. from the Milpitas USPS (450 S Abel St) via Priority Mail Flat Rate Envelope to Stockton, CA 95202 (San Joaquin Superior Court), USPS tracking 9505 5114 6005 6212 9832 68, postage $12.90, expected delivery Monday 08/03/2026 (USPS eReceipt email). Packets included the applicable POS-010 and all required default-judgment papers (CIV-100 Request for Entry of Default/Court Judgment, supporting Declaration, exhibits, and [Proposed] Judgment), seeking default judgment against each on a joint-and-several basis in an amount not less than $78,671.20 (Alpine on a successor-in-interest/alter ego/mere-continuation theory). As of the Aug. 1, 2026 5:40 PM FullCourt ROA printout, those July 31 mailings had not yet posted (last default-related ROA line remains the June 15 Not Entered entry) — consistent with expected delivery 08/03/2026 and clerk processing lag. No meet-and-confer outreach received from any defendant as of July 20, 2026 (meet-and-confer inapplicable per CM-110 — neither defendant has appeared). Renewed default judgment packets for Diamond and Alpine mailed July 31, 2026; awaiting ROA posting and clerk entry. Case assigned to Hon. Robert T. Waters, Department 11B for all purposes including trial. Case Management Statement (CM-110) filed July 20, 2026 (ROA 07/27/2026): stated default entered against Diamond (incorrect as to the ROA — June 15 request was Not Entered) and requests the Court conduct a default prove-up hearing against Diamond at or in connection with the CMC; discovery complete; case exempt from judicial arbitration/civil mediation because both defendants are in default or have not appeared (no opposing party available for ADR); 1-day jury trial estimate. Case Management Conference: 08/12/2026, 8:30 AM, Dept. 11B — clerk stated by phone that the CMC will be converted to a default prove-up hearing (bring renewed Diamond/Alpine packets and be prepared to proceed on affidavit under CCP §585(d) / CRC 3.1800). Jury trial demanded. POST-JUDGMENT COLLECTION PREP (as of July 29, 2026 — no judgment entered yet): EJ-001 (Abstract of Judgment), EJ-130 (Writ of Execution), AT-138/EJ-125 (Debtor Examination), and MC-012 (Memorandum of Costs) are pre-drafted with the fixed case/party/court facts filled in, ready to complete the same day or next business day once judgment actually enters — judgment-dependent fields (entry date, amount, hearing dates) are intentionally left blank rather than assumed. Alpine's joint-and-several liability runs through its own pre-drafted default judgment packet (CIV-100, execution date Aug. 1, 2026) — not a CCP §187 motion to amend the judgment to add an alter ego. §187 amendment is the wrong vehicle here: it exists to add an alter ego who was never a named party, and courts generally decline to use it where the underlying judgment was entered by default (no participation by the added party to satisfy due process). Alpine is already a named, personally-served defendant pursuing its own default judgment, so no §187 motion is needed or appropriate. DEFAULT JUDGMENT PACKET REVIEW (Jul. 29, 2026): (1) CASE NUMBER ERROR — Diamond's original CIV-100 (submitted 6/15/26; Not Entered) and the pre-correction Alpine draft both showed case number "STK-CV-UF-2026-1094" (missing the leading zeros of the actual "STK-CV-UF-2026-0001094") in every field where it appears; same defect was in the [Proposed] Judgment (JUD-100), now corrected in the file above. Diamond's CIV-100/Declaration were already submitted with this error — confirm with the clerk that the case was docketed correctly, since editing this record copy doesn't change what's already on file with the court;  The corrected Alpine packet (case number fixed to STK-CV-UF-2026-0001094) was among the complete packets Plaintiff mailed July 31, 2026 for both defendants. (2) JUD-100 STRUCTURAL GAP — original draft's Item 5a ("against defendant (names)") named only Diamond; Alpine's joint-and-several liability appeared solely in freeform Item 8 text, which the abstract of judgment (EJ-001) and writ (EJ-130) are not built to read — corrected version above adds Alpine to Item 5a and the DEFENDANT caption. (3) OSMANI vs. USMANI — Alpine's own Declaration ISO Default Judgment (¶6) cites "the same Osmani family ownership and management" as evidentiary support for the alter-ego/successor theory, but the only individual named anywhere in the service record is Usmani (spelled both "Mustagem" and "Mustaqem" across filings) — never "Osmani." This is a sworn statement supporting Alpine's liability that doesn't match the record; confirm and correct before it's relied on further. (4) STANDING QUESTION — the Lease-On Owner Operator Agreement underlying the $23,400 lost-income claim (Exhibit 4) is contractually between Gobbato Builders, LLC and "Altamont Freight LLC" (a separate registered business entity, per its own W-9 and Amazon Relay driver roster, at a different Modesto address), not personally Brendan Ngwa Nforbi — the Declaration frames the loss as his personally. Unlikely to be caught in an uncontested default prove-up, but worth resolving (e.g., confirming sole-member/alter-ego status) before this is relied on in a contested posture. (5) DMV fee vs. use-tax exemption — the $3,442 DMV fee claimed in full as damages includes ~$2,421 in CA use/city-use tax that a CDTFA exemption request (in the same exhibit set) sought to avoid on the ground the truck "was purchased outside of California"; the Declaration doesn't disclose whether that exemption was ever granted, which could reduce the true out-of-pocket DMV obligation.
damages: $53,671.20 (Aug 4, 2026 compensatory-only default prove-up): $20,218.65 documented out-of-pocket, $5,750.00 undocumented sworn losses, $23,400.00 conservative lost commercial income (18 wks × $1,300/wk), $4,302.55 prejudgment interest (Civ. Code §3287(a), 7%); costs waived; punitive damages omitted from this filing. Broader case-level range still extends higher if full trial-theory lost income (>$46,800) or later punitive/§425.115 notice is pursued; also includes disgorgement/restitution under UCL §17200 and postjudgment interest.
risk: Strong case: Diamond's fraud/concealment clearly pleaded; the alleged prior-owner disclosure could establish knowledge if confirmed; catastrophic defect objectively documented; damages quantifiable. Default judgment risk eliminated if Diamond responds before or at CMC. Punitive damages exposure substantial given willful conduct post-disclosure knowledge.
